cross_cutting_facts_established: CF1. The actual H1 price-bar span is 2020-01-29/30 .. 2026-09-02 (w1_freeze loader manifest), NOT 2018-09 despite snapshot filenames. Any trade (entry or exit fill) before 2020-01-30 is unfillable; under the inherited runner, entries before 2020-03-01 fall in the warmup region and receive NO fold.

CF2. The inherited frozen fold boundaries are (2020-03-01, 2022-05-01, 2024-07-01, 2026-09-02) = three folds F1 2020-03..2022-05, F2 2022-05..2024-07, F3 2024-07..2026-09 (scored_runner FOLD_BOUNDARIES, identical in V3 baseline_invariants). Fold schemes not expressible on this grid are runner-modifying deviations.

CF3. Deduped ledger event distribution by inherited folds (by effective_date and by first_readable_decision_utc, identical splits): pre-2020-03-01 = 8 events (AU 3, NZ 2, US 3) -> 26 pair-events; F1 = 21 events (AU 3, CA 5, GB 5, NZ 5, US 3) -> 39 pair-events; F2 = 70 events (AU 13, CA 9, CH 7, EMU 11, GB 11, JP 1, NZ 8, US 10) -> 130 pair-events; F3 = 52 events (AU 6, CA 8, CH 4, EMU 8, GB 6, JP 4, NZ 10, US 6) -> 88 pair-events. ZERO deduped events fall in 2020-01-30..2020-03-01.

CF4. Gross deduped pair-events for event-driven designs = 151 non-anchor multiplications: non-US areas 129 events x 1 pair + US 22 x 7 pairs = 283. Any packet counting from the raw 220-row file (212 rate changes) overstates by the 61 upgrade duplicates (e.g. 'AU 50' is 25 unique events; 'NZ 50' is 25; 'CH 22' is 11).

CF5. The 8 BASELINE_LEVEL rows carry effective_date = null, effective_time_utc = null, first_readable_decision_utc = null, operative_available_time_utc = 2019-01-01T23:59:59Z, status AVAILABILITY_UNEVIDENCED. The frozen-reader invariant (available_time_utc <= decision_ts AND effective_time_utc <= decision_ts) is NOT mechanically evaluable on these rows, and any use of baseline LEVELS to set an initial book state or open scored entries makes the 'provenance-only, non-load-bearing' claim false.

CF6. Cost kernel mechanics: tier books are re-bookings of the identical trade set at 2.25 / 3.0 bps per side with gross tier-invariant and STRESS_ROWS_NOT_DISTINCT refusal — NOT proportional scaling of net booked PnL. Packet prose saying 'applied to BOOKED stress PnL' is authoritative shorthand only where the packet also states the re-pricing semantics; prose describing proportional/loss scaling is mechanically wrong against the kernel.

CF7. Maximum inter-bar gap in the staged snapshot is <= 85h (gaps_gt_85h = [] on all 7 pairs), so a fill placed on the IMMEDIATE next bar after any 16:00-NY decision can never exceed the 4-day validator bound on this snapshot. The V3R abort was a 2-session-late fill (scheduling bug), not a calendar gap. Designs whose control books inherit the anchor's fill schedule byte-for-byte are structurally immune; designs that merely ASSERT the 4-day bound without a fail-closed path rely on implementation correctness, with the frozen validator abort as the only backstop.

CF8. Tier-2.0 is declared a PRIMARY Stage-A gate in all six packets (verified per packet, see per-proposal records). Base/tier arithmetic 1.5 bps/side x {1.0,1.5,2.0} -> 3.0/4.5/6.0 bps round trip is internally consistent in all six packets.

FXFV4-A4-P1.verdict_rationale: Mechanism, data citations, PIT semantics, cost arithmetic and control design are implementable with existing authorized data and the inherited kernel; the packet is runnable once its fold-scheme/window defects (F1/F2 below) are resolved by falling back to the inherited frozen boundaries it claims to inherit. Not DATA_BLOCKED: every cited series is citable. Not INFEASIBLE: no finding removes the ability to construct Delta_r, fill next-session, or run all arms on the staged snapshot.

findings.evidence: Packet states '3 folds on the inherited frozen boundaries (2020-03-01, 2022-05-01, end 2026-09-02)' and 'Fold 1 (2019-01..2020-03, ~14 months)'. The inherited frozen boundaries (scored_runner FOLD_BOUNDARIES) are 2020-03-01, 2022-05-01, 2024-07-01, 2026-09-02 — the packet drops the 2024-07-01 internal boundary, producing a non-inherited 4.3-year third fold. Moreover fold_of() returns None (warmup region) for entries before 2020-03-01, so a pre-2020-03 fold is not expressible on the inherited runner at all.
findings.consequence: Two mutually exclusive fold schemes: the packet's stated scheme (F1 pre-2020-03) is unimplementable on the frozen runner; under the inherited scheme the gate arithmetic (2-of-3 positive populated folds) degrades differently than the packet's ex-ante disclosure assumes. Implementation cannot be mechanical until D2/owner pins the scheme. The packet's own intent string ('inherited frozen boundaries') points to the inherited grid; under that reading the packet runs with degraded fold population rather than failing.

findings.evidence: Packet scores 'over 2019-01..2026-09' and estimates fold 1 as ~14 months of trading. Actual H1 bars start 2020-01-29/30 (w1_freeze loader manifest) and the inherited fold window starts 2020-03-01. CF3 shows ZERO deduped ledger events fall in 2020-01-30..2020-03-01.
findings.consequence: Fold 1 as described by the packet cannot exist: under the packet's own scheme it contains 0 event-driven trades (structurally unpopulated, gate degrades to 2-of-2 as the packet itself half-anticipates but with a ~14-month window that does not exist); under the inherited scheme the first fold (2020-03..2022-05) is itself knife-edge at the 30-trade populated floor (estimated 25-32 trades, see estimated_decision_counts). The 'honest_population_warning' materially understates the risk because it is anchored to a wrong window start.

findings.evidence: Packet evidence_class_per_row_group quotes raw-file fractions: 'AU rate changes: 25/50 rows EVIDENCED', 'NZ: 25/50', 'CH: 11/22', '112 AVAILABILITY_UNEVIDENCED rows total'. Per the pinned-ledger dedupe (last-row-wins), the operative state is AU 25/25, NZ 25/25, CH 11/11 evidenced (all 61 upgrade duplicates are UNEVIDENCED->EVIDENCED), with 43 deduped unevidenced rate-change rows + 8 baselines = 51 unevidenced rows, not 112. The same packet's own ledger summary ('220 rows ... 108 EVIDENCED') matches the deduped evidenced count, so the packet mixes raw and deduped counting conventions internally.
findings.consequence: Conservative direction (operative state is MORE evidenced than the packet claims; no P-1 violation — no asserted bounds), but an implementer keying availability gates to the packet's per-row-group text rather than to the ledger's last-row-wins semantics will mis-build the vintage reader. Mismatch is detectable at implementation (ledger re-hash + row-group tallies) and must be resolved in favor of the deduped ledger.

findings.evidence: Packet claims baseline rows are 'provenance-only and NOT computationally load-bearing (the level is constant at window start, so its availability cannot change any readable value inside the window)' and seeds 'w_booked seeded to w_target at the first populated clock without a fill'. w_target at that clock is computed FROM the baseline levels, and the seed state determines when the hysteresis trigger first fires (seed-to-target suppresses an immediate entry that a seed-from-zero convention would produce). Baseline rows are AVAILABILITY_UNEVIDENCED with effective_time_utc = null (CF5).
findings.consequence: The initialization IS load-bearing for the scored trade schedule, and it rests on unevidenced rows whose frozen-reader invariant is not mechanically evaluable. PIT-legality is not violated (the conservative bound 2019-01-01T23:59:59Z precedes any window), but the packet's non-load-bearing claim is false and the null effective_time handling forces an implementer judgment. The seed convention itself (seed = target vs seed = 0) is not stated as a frozen choice elsewhere in the packet.

findings.evidence: Packet estimates '120-220 trades' driven by 'the ~212 rate-change rows of the pinned ledger'. Deduped gross pair-events = 283 (CF4); 26 pre-price-window pair-events are unfillable; hysteresis (|dw| >= 0.10) plus saturation (w pegged at +/-1 while |Delta_r| >= 48 bps, e.g. EMU-US stays between -87 and -238 bps from baseline through 2026-06, so all 19 EMU events and most US hikes fire no trade on EUR/USD) suppress an estimated 40-55% of fillable pair-events. Estimated total round trips 95-155, fold split (inherited scheme) ~25-32 / ~40-70 / ~40-60.
findings.consequence: The expected-decision band is overstated roughly 1.5-2x. The per-arm 40-decision floor is met with margin (decisions ~= fillable pair-events ~= 257), but fold populations sit at or near the 30-trade populated floor in the first inherited fold, and the full-sample outcome may land below the packet's band floor of 120.

findings.evidence: Packet asserts 'The decision-to-fill gap is exactly one session (1-4 calendar days across weekends/holidays), always inside the frozen validator's next-session/4-day constraint' with no fail-closed >4-day path specified. CF7 shows the assertion holds on this snapshot (gaps_gt_85h = []) provided fills go to the immediate next bar; the V3R abort was a scheduling bug, not a calendar gap. The control arm's fill schedule is byte-identical to the anchor's, so a validator abort, if it ever occurred, would hit both arms identically.
findings.consequence: Residual risk is implementation correctness of 'first session bar strictly after the decision clock', backstopped by the frozen validator. An explicit fail-closed NO_TRADE path (as in the A6 packets) would remove the residual ambiguity; as written, a >4-day condition has unspecified behavior.

findings.evidence: costs.stress_tiers says 'multipliers x1.5 and x2.0 applied to BOOKED stress PnL (F1-fixed convention)' and immediately also 'tier books re-price every fill at 2.25 / 3.0 bps per side'. The kernel (book_stress) implements the re-pricing semantics with gross tier-invariant (CF6); literal proportional scaling of net booked PnL would make the tier-2.0 gate sign-preserved from base and contradict the ancestor's observed base-positive/tier-2.0-negative outcome.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic is internally consistent (C_rt(tier2.0) = 6.0 bps; kappa = 2 x 6 x 252/63 = 48 bps verified; SAFETY=3 neighbour kappa = 72 bps verified; carry-at-kappa = 12 bps = 2 x RT verified). Only the 'applied to BOOKED stress PnL' phrasing is ambiguous; the re-pricing sentence governs and matches the kernel.

Handling of null effective_time_utc on BASELINE_LEVEL rows inside the frozen-reader invariant (A4P1-M2).
Behavior if a decision's next-bar gap ever exceeded 4 days: no fail-closed path specified (A4P1-L1).

FXFV4-A5-P1.verdict_rationale: The blocker is real and accurately specified: the inflation leg (cpi_bis_ws_long_cpi) is STAGED_NOT_CITABLE with availability evidence NOT WIRED per p2_data_authority_v4.json, and the catalog explicitly rules it 'NOT citable by V4 D1 proposals'; the alternative (cpi_ecb_icp) is NOT_FUNDED for 7 of 8 areas. The mechanism genuinely cannot be constructed PIT-honestly today, so DATA_BLOCKED is the correct disposition and the packet is a valid FOREX_FREE_V4_BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION candidate. Findings below qualify the frozen unblock-time spec, not the blocker's validity.

findings.evidence: Blocker claims verified against the catalog: cpi_bis_ws_long_cpi STAGED_NOT_CITABLE, probe M.AU 92 monthly obs 2018-11..2026-06 keyless, 'probe bytes archived at /tmp probe only (not staged)'; consequence 'NOT citable by V4 D1 proposals'. The packet's unblock path (per-print official release-calendar ledger rows with archive hashes for BLS/ONS/ABS/StatsNZ/StatCan/FSO/SBJ/Eurostat, precision INSTANT or conservative DAY, then re-pin, regenerate vintages, re-run P2, upgrade status) matches the catalog's requirement and the existing ledger-extension tooling (announcement_archives_v4_extension/, announcement_ledger_builder_v4_extension.py present in the run tree).
findings.consequence: Blocker spec accurate; unblock path correct and sufficient in principle. Two nits: (a) constraint_compliance says 'BIS WS_LONG_CPI already staged per P2 authority' while the catalog records the probe bytes as NOT staged (/tmp only) — the series body is re-fetchable but nothing is staged; (b) the inherited vintage pipeline is daily-rates-oriented; monthly reference_price_month -> announcement_date semantics are specified in the packet but are genuine new implementation work at unblock time.

findings.evidence: folds_plan specifies 'purge gap = 20 sessions' while the inherited runner freezes PURGE_DAYS = 14 (calendar days); sample_floor uses a 12-trade fold-population floor while the inherited FOLD_POPULATED_MIN_TRADES = 30 and sibling packet A5-P2 uses 30; costs.application describes 'proportional scaling of each trade's booked PnL' and margin notes describe 'x1.5 loss scaling on losers' while the kernel re-books at tiered per-side costs with gross tier-invariant (CF6).
findings.consequence: Three frozen-convention deviations/conflicts inside one packet. If unblocked and run 'EXACTLY as frozen here' (the packet's own commitment), the runner and the packet would disagree on purge width, fold floor, and stress mechanics; implementation would face non-mechanical choices. These must be reconciled before any unblock cycle.

findings.evidence: Packet expects 'approximately 1750 [decisions] per pair (2019-01..2026-09 minus 252-session warmup)'. With actual bars from 2020-01-30 (CF1), the post-warmup window is ~2021-02..2026-09 ~= 1,430 sessions per pair. Band-crossing trades '6-14 per pair' shrink proportionally to ~5-12; the 60-trade full-sample floor is inside the shrunken band (35-84) rather than merely 'band-caveat' territory.
findings.consequence: Decision floor (100/packet, 40 frozen) comfortably met either way, but the 60-populated-anchor-trades floor becomes a coin flip; SAMPLE_FLOOR_FAIL is a live modal outcome the packet partially anticipates via band_caveat.

findings.evidence: pit_observable correctly states the policy-rate leg is citable only with pinned-ledger semantics and that unevidenced rows are read 'only ever read at the later bound'; placebo algebra D_placebo = D + 2*(pi_b - pi_q) verified correct; control shares the anchor's daily clock and next-session fills so it runs under evidenced semantics (no refused-control path).
findings.consequence: Availability discipline and control design are sound; the control-reproduction gate (>= 90% overlap -> inflation channel non-causal) is mechanically checkable.

findings.dimension: schedule definition ambiguity (must be fixed before any unblock)
findings.evidence: decision_clock.event reads: 'for each pair, the first FX session whose 16:00 America/New_York decision timestamp falls strictly after BOTH areas' latest CPI print evidenced availability stamps, and at least one full session after each print (one-event-lag rule)'. Read literally this condition is satisfied by EVERY session after the latest print (i.e. a daily clock), not a monthly one; the packet elsewhere claims 'MONTHLY ... ~57 monthly decision events per pair' and 'first post-print session 16:00-NY per pair'.
findings.consequence: The decision clock is not mechanically implementable as written: 'monthly' cadence needs an explicit anchor (first qualifying session after each new print, or first qualifying session per calendar month). The one-event-lag qualifier is correct against the V3R precedent, but the cadence definition would force an implementer judgment on every session. This does not invalidate the DATA_BLOCKED disposition; it must be repaired in the frozen memo before any unblock cycle.

findings.evidence: Packet expects '~57 monthly decision events per pair (93-month window minus 36-month warmup)' and '160-280 pair-month trades' from 'band entries expected in 40-70% of pair-months' against floors of 120 full-sample trades and 30/fold. Actual price span 2020-01-30..2026-09-02 (CF1) ~= 79.5 months; minus the 36-month warmup ~= 43-44 monthly decisions per pair ~= 300-310 pair-months; 40-70% -> ~120-215 trades.
findings.consequence: The 120-trade full-sample floor moves from 'comfortable' to knife-edge at the low end of the packet's own band; fold counts (inherited grid, ~1/3 each) land ~40-72 — above the 30/fold floor only in mid-band. SAMPLE_FLOOR_FAIL is a realistic modal outcome.

findings.evidence: holding_period.exit_conditions contains garbled text: 'or early exit when q re-crosses toward Q by at least half the entry deviation at a decision event' — the entry_exit_rules.exit field says only 'per holding_period exit conditions'. The band constants are consistent (band_log_points 0.02 = 2% log deviation; state_rule thresholds q >= Q + 0.02 / q <= Q - 0.02).
findings.consequence: The early-exit rule (the only exit besides expiry and fold force-flat) is not stated in implementable form. Must be rewritten as a mechanical condition before unblock.

findings.evidence: folds_plan 'purge gap = 21 sessions' vs frozen PURGE_DAYS = 14; sample_floor fold floor 30 matches the frozen FOLD_POPULATED_MIN_TRADES = 30 (unlike sibling P1's 12); costs.application 'proportional scaling of each trade's booked PnL' vs kernel re-booking at tiered per-side costs (CF6).
findings.consequence: Purge width and stress-application prose conflict with the frozen kernel; fold floor happens to match. Reconcile before unblock.

findings.evidence: Blocker verified accurate (catalog: STAGED_NOT_CITABLE / NOT WIRED / NOT_FUNDED for the alternative; consequence NOT citable by V4 D1 proposals). The stale-mismatch placebo reads P(quote, t-12m) — an OLDER evidenced read is always PIT-legal, so the control runs to completion under evidenced semantics; the packet's own margin note honestly discloses that low-inflation subperiods may drive >= 90% anchor/control overlap and accepts the frozen rule anyway.
findings.consequence: Blocker valid; control design legal and runnable at unblock time.

FXFV4-A6-P1.verdict_rationale: Price-only mechanism on the authorized H1 snapshot; no macro availability dependency; decision clock daily at a completed-bar instant; next-session fills with an explicit >4-day fail-closed NO_TRADE path (the strongest validator-precedent compliance of the six packets); sham-bloc control runs by construction; frozen constants quoted verbatim match the runner; fold boundaries quoted match the inherited grid exactly.

findings.evidence: F1 (2020-03-01..2022-05-01) population estimated by the packet at 1.0-1.8x the 30-trade floor (30-54). Warmup (60 valid NY-days from 2020-01-30) puts first decisions in early May 2020, so effective F1 decisions span ~2020-05..2022-05; the COVID risk-off cluster dominates this span. Auditor estimate: at the packet's own event frequency (z <= -1 on 10-16% of NY-days) F1 holds ~540 valid decision days -> ~54-86 event days -> after 5-day hold overlap, ~60-120 leg-entries — comfortably populated, but the packet's own thinner estimate shows the design anticipates population thinness.
findings.consequence: Fold 1 populated in either estimate; the packet's disclosure (THIN, INDETERMINATE risk acknowledged) is adequate. No structural risk, but a sub-30 outcome remains possible if realized event frequency lands at the bottom of the band with heavy overlap.

findings.evidence: Drop-one design uses 6 scenarios (5 leg-drops + best-fold drop) with a 5-of-6 survival gate, described as a 'proportional tightening of the inherited M1-DEV 6/8 rule'. The frozen harness constant is DROPOUT_SCENARIOS = 8, DROPOUT_MIN_SURVIVAL = 6 (ratio 0.75; the proposed 5/6 = 0.833 is tighter). The design reason is sound (EUR/GBP are not traded legs; only 5 pair-drops are meaningful) and the packet explicitly warns 'asserted at implementation as a test'.
findings.consequence: A deviation from the frozen 8-scenario denominator with disclosed, tightening-only effect. Implementation must either parameterize the dropout harness for 6 scenarios or map the 5 leg-drops into the inherited harness; either is mechanical, but it is runner-adjacent work the packet should have costed. Leg-drop non-vacuity is genuinely satisfied (dropping a trigger leg changes S_t; dropping a response leg changes the basket), so drop-one meaningfulness is preserved.

findings.evidence: Fill convention: next-session 16:00-NY bar open, 'at most 4 calendar days later over holiday weekends ... a fill gap that would exceed 4 days fails closed to NO_TRADE'; session gate Sun 21:00 -> Fri 16:00 NY; missing bars fail closed (NO_EVAL / earliest-scheduled exit, never fill-forward). This is the exact discipline the V3R ONE_EVENT_LAG_VIOLATION demands, plus a fail-closed path the A4/A5 packets lack.
findings.consequence: Validator-clean by construction and by explicit failure path; control (sham EUR/GBP bloc) and benchmark (t-10 trigger) inherit the same machinery and cannot be refused.

findings.evidence: pit_observable cites 'frozen span 2020-01-30..2026-09-02 (research/control/forex_free_v4_run/p2_data_authority_v4.json: price_series_byte_replay 152/152 identical...)'. The byte-replay verdict is indeed in p2_data_authority_v4.json, but the span itself is recorded in the w1_freeze loader manifest, not in p2. Decisions estimate ~1,450 NY-days per leg slightly undercounts the ~1,600 post-warmup NY-days; harmless vs floors (satisfied by two orders of magnitude).
findings.consequence: Cosmetic citation misattribution; all substantive numbers check out.

No other material ambiguities found: trigger signs, standardization window, threshold semantics (z == -1.0 fires, <= frozen), governor, fold force-flat, and benchmark staleness are all stated mechanically.

Feasible, with the turnover-basis finding below thinning the disclosed floor margins.

findings.dimension: coverage/turnover arithmetic on raw vs deduped ledger
findings.evidence: Packet counts '212 RATE_CHANGE across AU 50, NZ 50, CA 22, CH 22, GB 22, US 22, EMU 19, JP 5' -> 'non-US areas 190 + US 22x7 = 344 pair-events gross; ... est. 290-315 decisions remain' and F1 population 'est. 1.5-2.7x the 30-trade floor'. The operative deduped ledger has 151 rate changes (AU 25, NZ 25, CH 11 unique — the 50/50/22 figures are raw rows including the 61 UNEVIDENCED->EVIDENCED upgrade duplicates): gross pair-events = 129 + 154 = 283; pre-snapshot NO_EVAL removes ~26-31; within-hold (10 NY-day) flat-only suppression removes ~10-20 (e.g. the second 2020-03 US cut is ignored on all 7 pairs). Estimated decisions ~240-255; estimated scored trades ~200-230 — inside the packet's 180-260 trades band, but the per-fold consequence is material: inherited F1 contains 21 deduped events -> 39 pair-events -> after double-cut suppression ~21-27 trades, AT/BELOW the 30-trade populated floor (the packet's 45-81 was computed on raw counts).
findings.consequence: The 140-trade full-sample floor survives (margin ~1.4-1.6x, thinner than the disclosed 1.3-1.9x on a larger base is roughly equivalent); the per-arm 40-decision floor survives; but F1 flips from 'comfortably populated' to 'likely unpopulated', degrading the fold gate to 2-of-2. The packet's INDETERMINATE-not-negative rule would make this a population outcome, not a mechanistic one. The conservative direction of dedupe (upgrades only ADD evidence) means no availability risk — purely a counting-basis error.

findings.evidence: 8-scenario suite (7 pair-drops + best-fold) matches the frozen DROPOUT_SCENARIOS = 8 / DROPOUT_MIN_SURVIVAL = 6 verbatim. The packet itself discloses that dropping USD/JPY removes only ~5 trades (JP has exactly 5 deduped events, 2024-03..2026-06 — verified) making that scenario near-vacuous 'by data scarcity, not by design', and that the gate 'can only detect pair-concentration through the other 6 pairs'.
findings.consequence: Disclosure is accurate and the suite is compliant; the effective denominator for meaningful pair-drops is 6-7 of 8 while the gate stays at 6 — an announced weakening of detection power, not a feasibility defect.

findings.evidence: Eligibility rule (decision instant T = first completed 16:00-NY bar completion >= operative_available_time_utc; never eligible on effective date alone; rows without stamps fail closed MISSING_AVAILABLE_TIME_EVIDENCE) matches the pinned-ledger semantics; measured median effective->readable lag ~1.8 days is consistent with the ledger's first_readable_decision_utc values (auditor spot-check). The claim 'every ledger row carries operative_available_time_utc / first_readable_decision_utc' is literally false for the 8 BASELINE_LEVEL rows (both null), but this family reads only RATE_CHANGE rows, on which the claim holds.
findings.consequence: Semantics correct on the rows actually used; the universal quantifier is a wording nit. Tie-break (earlier availability instant wins) is mechanical.

findings.dimension: schedule breadth / validator precedent + benchmark edge effects
findings.evidence: Fill convention: next-session 16:00-NY bar, fail-closed NO_TRADE if the gap would exceed 4 days; one-event-lag satisfied; control's decisions are driven by the same availability instants as the anchor with a different pair map, so its fill chain is validator-identical (CF7). The +180d stale-event benchmark shifts late-window events past 2026-09-02 (the last ~6 months of events have no stale twin), shrinking the benchmark book asymmetrically — an accepted consequence of the frozen constant, disclosed as 'schedule shape unchanged' only approximately.
findings.consequence: Validator-clean; incremental-alpha comparison remains well-defined (both books scored on the same window); the asymmetry is a diagnostic caveat, not a feasibility issue.

ambiguities: None blocking. Minor: the deterministic tie-break resolves same-instant events per pair, but events from DIFFERENT areas mapping to the same pair at DIFFERENT availability instants inside an open 10-day hold are silently ignored (no queueing) — stated ('no refresh'), mechanical.

Warmup statement 'events whose first decision instant falls before 2020-02-11 (snapshot start + one session + lag) are NO_EVAL' fixes a concrete cutoff — mechanical, though the +12-day offset is a convention choice stated as frozen.

limitations: data_raw/forex_free_v1 is absent in this worktree (gitignored); price coverage was audited from research/control/forex_free_v1_run/staged_data_manifest.json (156 digests) and the w1_freeze loader manifest (per-pair bar spans, gap checks), cross-checked against the A6 packets' span claims. No price bytes were read.

Trade/decision counts are light-arithmetic estimates from the deduped ledger event distribution, snapshot spans, and stated mechanism constants (hysteresis/saturation, hold horizons, band frequencies). They are bounds for floor-checking, not simulations; no schedule was generated and no price series was touched.
The A6-P1 event-frequency band (10-16% of NY-days) and A5 band-crossing estimates are taken from the packets as design priors; the audit checked their internal consistency, not their empirical truth.

Verdict FEASIBLE is a data/design-feasibility ruling only: it says the packet can be implemented and run to completion on authorized data under the frozen kernel/validator. It predicates no outcome on any Stage-A gate, and several gates are independently disclosed by the packets as knife-edge or likely-fail (e.g. A6-P2 USD-drift, A4 stress-tier margins).

The A4 fold-scheme findings (A4P1-H1/A4P2-H1) admit two readings; this audit rules the inherited FOLD_BOUNDARIES authoritative because both packets explicitly claim to inherit them, and records the deviation as the finding rather than silently adopting either scheme.

Ledger analysis used the documented last-row-wins dedupe by (area, effective_date); the 61 duplicates were verified to be exclusively UNEVIDENCED->EVIDENCED upgrades, so dedupe is evidence-monotone and the conservative direction of all packet evidence claims is preserved.
This audit writes only research/audits/forex_free_v4/ artifacts and repairs nothing.
